The employee who completes the most jobs isn't automatically the strongest performer.

Team benchmarks, recent trends, and consistency over time can add important context to individual results. Comparing several measures helps managers ask better questions about performance.

My Field Team Performance Power BI Kit includes a dedicated Employee Performance dashboard: https://garrettsdevdesk.etsy.com/listing/4595448076/power-bi-field-team-performance

Finishing a field service job is important. Understanding whether the work holds up matters, too.

Repeat visits, restoration time, and customer commitments can help reveal service reliability issues that completion totals alone might miss.

Try reviewing your field team's completed jobs alongside repeat work and service timing. Look for patterns worth investigating, especially where high activity coincides with recurring quality concerns.

Where does your field team's workday actually go?

Comparing completed activities with labor hours can provide a useful productivity measure. Adding billable output and quality information gives that measure more context, especially when different jobs require different amounts of effort.

My Field Team Performance Power BI Kit includes a Field Activity & Productivity dashboard: https://garrettsdevdesk.etsy.com/listing/4595448076/power-bi-field-team-performance

A productive field team needs more than a packed schedule.

Completion rates, labor efficiency, repeat work, and service reliability each reveal something different about performance. Looking at these measures together can help managers understand whether the team is delivering results sustainably.

For anyone managing field operations or service teams, which measure tells you the most about whether your team is performing well?
